name: Question 9
problem:
The substitution $z={y}^{m}$ for some integer $m$ transforms the differential equation

$$
{x}^{2}\,\frac{dy}{dx}-y(2x+3{y}^{2})=0
$$

into an equation of the form ${z}^{′}(x)+P(x)z(x)=Q(x).$ What is the function $Q(x)?$
worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\,\frac{dy}{dx}-y(2x+3{y}^{2}) & =0 \\ {x}^{2}\,\frac{dy}{dx}-2xy-3{y}^{3} & =0 \\ {x}^{2}\,\frac{dy}{dx}-2xy & =3{y}^{3} \\ \frac{dy}{dx}-2{x}^{-1}y & =3{x}^{-2}{y}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that our equation is an instance of the Bernoulli differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dx}+p(x)y=q(x){y}^{n}.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
p(x)=-2{x}^{-1},\,q(x)=3{x}^{-2},\,n=3.
$$

Now, we divide the differential equation by ${y}^{3},$ and we get

$$
{y}^{-3}\frac{dy}{dx}-2{x}^{-1}{y}^{-2}=3{x}^{-2}.\,\,(∗)
$$

Then, we make the substitution

$$
z={y}^{1-n}={y}^{-2}.
$$

Differentiating $z(x)$ using the chain rule, we get 

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}=-2{y}^{-3}\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,⟹\,{y}^{-3}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=-\frac{1}{2}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}.
$$

 

Therefore, equation $(∗)$ can be written as a linear equation in $z(x)$ as follows:

$$
-\frac{1}{2}\,\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}-2{x}^{-1}z=3{x}^{-2}
$$

Finally, we write the above equation in standard form, which gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+4{x}^{-1}z=-6{x}^{-2}.
$$

Therefore, $Q(x)=-6{x}^{-2}.$

Question 9
?

The substitution z=ym for some integer m transforms the differential equation x2dydx−y(2x+3y2)=0 into an equation of the form z′(x)+P(x)z(x)=Q(x). What is the function Q(x)?

a
 −6x−2
b
 −6x−1
c
 4x−1
d
 2x−2
e
 −3x−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we rearrange the equation, as follows: x2dydx−y(2x+3y2)=0x2dydx−2xy−3y3=0x2dydx−2xy=3y3dydx−2x−1y=3x−2y3

Notice that our equation is an instance of the Bernoulli differential equation

dydx+p(x)y=q(x)yn.

In this case, we have

p(x)=−2x−1,q(x)=3x−2,n=3.

Now, we divide the differential equation by y3, and we get y−3dydx−2x−1y−2=3x−2.(∗)

Then, we make the substitution z=y1−n=y−2.

Differentiating z(x) using the chain rule, we get dzdx=−2y−3dydx⟹y−3dydx=−12dzdx.

Therefore, equation (∗) can be written as a linear equation in z(x) as follows: −12dzdx−2x−1z=3x−2 Finally, we write the above equation in standard form, which gives dzdx+4x−1z=−6x−2. Therefore, Q(x)=−6x−2.
